diagnosis.cause: No rule recognises this failure (run with --brain auto to ask IBM Bob).

`numpy==1.17.0` is pinned, and PyPI only has builds of it up to Python 3.7; on Python 3.12 it tries to compile from source and fails. The docs don't say which Python to use. Pinning the rest of the install to Python 3.7's own era too, so the build toolchain (setuptools/Cython) matches instead of today's.

runtime.name: python
runtime.source: newest Python with a numpy==1.17.0 wheel on PyPI

actions.command: pip install "cython<3.0" "setuptools<58" wheel && pip install --no-build-isolation -r requirements.txt

doc.text: Python 3.7 (the pinned numpy==1.17.0 has no build for newer Python)
